Vendor Stability.content:
OneTrust was founded in 2016 by Kabir Barday in Atlanta, Georgia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OneTrust). The company has raised over $1.13 billion in total venture funding across multiple investment rounds (https://tracxn.com/d/companies/onetrust/__ze9yaIbvxYzoxTM_yqDNZtaDbQ_ItyTV7ebRehscTWI): a $200 million Series A in July 2019 led by Insight Partners at a $1.3 billion valuation (https://www.clay.com/dossier/onetrust-funding); a $210 million Series B in February 2020 led by Coatue at a $2.7 billion valuation (https://www.clay.com/dossier/onetrust-funding); a $300 million Series C in December 2020 led by TCV at a $5.1 billion valuation (https://www.clay.com/dossier/onetrust-funding); a $210 million Series C extension in April 2021 (https://tracxn.com/d/companies/onetrust/__ze9yaIbvxYzoxTM_yqDNZtaDbQ_ItyTV7ebRehscTWI); and a $150 million Series D in July 2023 led by Generation Investment Management and Sands Capital at a $4.5 billion valuation (https://tracxn.com/d/companies/onetrust/__ze9yaIbvxYzoxTM_yqDNZtaDbQ_ItyTV7ebRehscTWI).

As of 2026, OneTrust maintains a global workforce of approximately 2,487 employees (https://tracxn.com/d/companies/onetrust/__ze9yaIbvxYzoxTM_yqDNZtaDbQ_ItyTV7ebRehscTWI). In June 2022, the company laid off roughly 950 employees (25% of its workforce) to pivot toward profitability amidst changing market conditions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OneTrust). Founder Kabir Barday continues to lead the firm as CEO (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OneTrust), with no critical public leadership departures reported ("no URL available for this"). There are no active shutdown rumors or indications of financial distress ("no URL available for this"). Instead of being an acquisition target, OneTrust acts as an aggressive consolidator, acquiring companies such as DataGuidance, Integris Software, Docuvision, Tugboat Logic, Convercent, and Planetly (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OneTrust).
Vendor Stability.source_type: self-reported, corroborated by named funding/board sources

Incident History.content:
In June 2026, OneTrust experienced a supply-chain security incident involving a third-party app integration (Klue Battlecards) that allowed an unauthorized threat actor to compromise OAuth tokens and view sales data in OneTrust's internal Salesforce CRM (https://www.onetrust.com/blog/update-from-onetrust-on-klue-salesforce-security-incident/). Forensic investigation confirmed that customer-managed OneTrust production tenant environments, customer databases, and production workflows were completely unimpacted by this event (https://www.onetrust.com/blog/update-from-onetrust-on-klue-salesforce-security-incident/).

No direct data breaches involving production customer databases have occurred ("no URL available for this"). OneTrust's cloud platform reports stable availability, though some enterprise customers note that automated web cookie crawlers can occasionally generate heavy traffic spikes on host sites during discovery scans (https://www.enzuzo.com/blog/onetrust-review). There are no major public lawsuits or regulatory enforcement actions against OneTrust related to data mishandling or security flaws ("no URL available for this").

Community Signal.content:
Across major peer review platforms, OneTrust receives solid product ratings but mixed feedback regarding pricing (https://www.enzuzo.com/blog/onetrust-review):

	•	G2: Rated 4.4 out of 5 across 280+ reviews, with high ratings for Tech Risk & Compliance (4.6/5) and Privacy Automation (4.3/5) (https://www.enzuzo.com/blog/onetrust-review). 
	•	Capterra: Holds a 4.3 out of 5 overall score across 56 reviews (https://www.enzuzo.com/blog/onetrust-review). 
	•	Trustpilot: Holds a low 1.5 out of 5 rating across 28 reviews, driven almost entirely by pricing and renewal terms (https://www.enzuzo.com/blog/onetrust-review). 
On Reddit, Hacker News, and practitioner forums, users frequently praise OneTrust for its comprehensive module depth, regulatory research capabilities via DataGuidance, and broad international compliance framework coverage (https://www.enzuzo.com/blog/onetrust-review). Conversely, the most persistent complaints center on platform complexity, long setup timelines requiring professional services, opaque sales-driven pricing, and steep renewal cost increases (https://www.enzuzo.com/blog/onetrust-review) (https://consently.net/blog/onetrust-review). Mid-market buyers frequently report migrating to lighter compliance and consent alternatives (such as Ketch, Osano, Vanta, or Drata) to avoid high entry contracts ($10,000/year minimum) (https://www.enzuzo.com/blog/onetrust-review).

Compliance Posture.content:
•	SOC 2 Status: OneTrust maintains an active SOC 2 Type II report covering Security, Availability, and Confidentiality (https://my.onetrust.com/s/article/UUID-21f6bff2-1b12-8c67-e8b0-d852e36f37af) (https://www-onetrust-com.proxy.uchicago.edu/trust/). This claim is independently audited and verified ("no URL available for this"). 
	•	ISO Certifications: OneTrust holds ISO/IEC 27001 (Information Security Management) and ISO/IEC 27701 (Privacy Information Management) certifications (https://my.onetrust.com/s/article/UUID-21f6bff2-1b12-8c67-e8b0-d852e36f37af). These certifications are independently confirmed by Coalfire ISO, an ANAB and UKAS accredited certification body (https://www.onetrust.com/news/onetrust-achieves-worlds-first-iso-27701/). 
	•	GDPR: Built natively around General Data Protection Regulation requirements; vendor self-claim confirmed by public platform documentation (https://www.enzuzo.com/blog/onetrust-review) (https://www.onetrust.com/news/onetrust-achieves-worlds-first-iso-27701/). 
	•	HIPAA / BAA: OneTrust offers a specialized US-hosted HIPAA cloud environment and executes formal Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) for organizations handling Protected Health Information (PHI) (https://my.onetrust.com/s/article/UUID-c53ae2d6-ac12-1713-6d7c-fa12c560c3fc). 
	•	PCI DSS: OneTrust is not a payment processor, but operates on cloud hosting infrastructure that satisfies PCI DSS standards ("no URL available for this"). 
	•	FedRAMP: OneTrust utilizes Microsoft Azure infrastructure with FedRAMP accreditation (https://my.onetrust.com/s/article/UUID-21f6bff2-1b12-8c67-e8b0-d852e36f37af); however, the OneTrust application itself is not currently listed as an independently authorized FedRAMP service on the official FedRAMP Marketplace ("no URL available for this").

Data Handling Posture.content:
OneTrust collects customer administrative metadata, user access details, risk evaluation records, Data Subject Access Requests (DSARs), consent records, and third-party vendor assessment documentation (https://www.enzuzo.com/blog/onetrust-review) (https://my.onetrust.com/s/article/UUID-9743079f-da29-65f6-17ee-ff518e05c4b7). Primary SaaS tenant data is hosted on Microsoft Azure with regional choices across the United States, Canada, Brazil, United Kingdom, Europe, Australia, and Asia (https://my.onetrust.com/s/article/UUID-21f6bff2-1b12-8c67-e8b0-d852e36f37af). Select acquired components (such as Tugboat Logic or Planetly) are hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS) in the US, Canada, Europe, and Germany (https://my.onetrust.com/s/article/UUID-21f6bff2-1b12-8c67-e8b0-d852e36f37af).

System backups on Microsoft Azure are maintained continuously (full backups weekly, differential every 12–24 hours, and transactional logs every 5–10 minutes) with a 14-day retention window, and stored encrypted with AES-256 (https://my.onetrust.com/s/article/UUID-21f6bff2-1b12-8c67-e8b0-d852e36f37af) (https://my.onetrust.com/articles/es/Knowledge/UUID-21f6bff2-1b12-8c67-e8b0-d852e36f37af). OneTrust does not use customer tenant data to train public or foundational artificial intelligence models without explicit user consent (https://privacyportal.onetrust.com/webform/ee5f2be9-45a3-41f1-bea3-082ff8a4f1a3/97c14c4f-b3f8-4e89-9b64-6bf4208e39b2). Approved subprocessors include Microsoft Azure, regional corporate affiliates (e.g., OneTrust LLC, OneTrust Technology Limited, OT Privacy Software Pvt Ltd), and operational tool providers (https://my.onetrust.com/s/article/List-of-Subprocessors?language=en_US).

Integration Risk.content:
OneTrust provides integration capabilities through REST APIs, Webhooks, mobile/web SDKs, and no-code connectors for enterprise platforms like Salesforce, Jira, and cloud infrastructure storage (https://developer.onetrust.com/onetrust/reference/onetrust-api-reference) (https://www.enzuzo.com/blog/onetrust-review). Customers can export data (including risk registers, data inventories, and assessment logs) in CSV or Excel formats using built-in UI tools or bulk API endpoints (https://my.onetrust.com/s/article/UUID-905f3684-6fe9-3534-d0ef-410de26ee801?topicId=0TO1Q000000ItSyWAK) (https://developer.onetrust.com/onetrust/reference/onetrust-api-reference).

API updates and release note changes require routine tracking, with periodic breaking changes reported during major module migration releases (https://developer.onetrust.com/onetrust/reference/onetrust-api-reference). The platform maintains a primary infrastructure dependency on Microsoft Azure and AWS (https://my.onetrust.com/s/article/UUID-21f6bff2-1b12-8c67-e8b0-d852e36f37af). Vendor lock-in risk is moderate to high due to the proprietary structure of custom risk frameworks, historical consent logs, custom questionnaires, and deeply integrated data mapping workflows (https://www.enzuzo.com/blog/onetrust-review).
